signals.title: OpenExecutive: open-source 'AI CEO' backed by 8 specialist Claude agents
signals.summary: After a CEO fired developers to make room for AI, they built and open-sourced a self-hosted virtual executive persona backed by 8 specialist Claude sub-agents (FastAPI + Next.js); 504 HN points, 321 comments, the loudest thread of the week.
signals.run_with_it_note: Clone the repo, drop in an Anthropic API key, run `make dev`, and feed it one business's numbers plus this week's morning-brief output. See if the 'executive' catches anything the brief missed.

signals.title: Perplexity + Nvidia ship Portable Computer: a fully local AI agent with zero token costs
signals.summary: Runs Qwen 3.8 27B and PPLX 27B entirely on-device on an Nvidia DGX Spark or any RTX GPU with 24GB+ VRAM, with app connectors and a security sandbox bundled in; no billing, no cloud round-trip unless the user approves an escalation. Windows lands in September.
signals.run_with_it_note: Price a used RTX 3090 (24GB, ~$700-900 secondhand) and run one always-on job locally, e.g. a nightly GBP-review scan across the 12 businesses, to see if local quality clears the bar to retire that cloud API call.

signals.title: GLM-5.3-Flash ships with open weights, closing last week's delay
signals.summary: Z.ai released the fast/cheap GLM-5.3-Flash variant with open weights, two weeks after gating the flagship's release on a cyber-capability safety score (last week's watch item). 995 HN points.
signals.run_with_it_note: Swap one low-stakes automated job (a summarization or triage step) onto GLM-5.3-Flash for a week and compare quality and cost against the current model.

signals.title: Nvidia agrees to acquire Hugging Face for $13B
signals.summary: The single biggest HN story of the week (948 points, 402 comments): the de facto neutral home for open model weights and datasets is being bought by the biggest AI chip vendor.

signals.title: AWS acquires DuckLabs, the company behind DuckDB
signals.summary: Top HN story of the week (1040 points); a bootstrapped, founder-owned open-source database company sells to AWS after 5 years, with DuckDB staying MIT-licensed under a nonprofit foundation.

signals.title: Apple ships M6 Mac mini and M5 Ultra Mac Studio, built for local AI dev
signals.summary: First 2nm Apple silicon (M6) and the new M5 Ultra; Mac mini starts at $899/16GB, Mac Studio at $2,499, both leaning on unified memory for local inference workloads.

signals.title: Launch HN: Vendo (YC S26), let users build features on top of your product
signals.summary: Embeddable SDK letting a SaaS's own users build custom features on top of the product; surfaced in two separate HN searches this week, 61 points.

signals.title: Show HN: OzBrain, a shared brain for knowledge between agents and your team
signals.summary: Small Show HN (92 points) pitching a shared memory layer so multiple AI agents and a human team stay in sync on the same facts.

signals.title: Amazon Mechanical Turk shutting down September 30
signals.summary: The original human-microwork marketplace closes; 307 HN points. A quiet marker that AI agents have eaten most of the demand for cheap human piecework.

signals.title: Stripe acquires Clerky
signals.summary: Stripe adds startup legal/cap-table tooling (Clerky) to its portfolio, days after its $7B OpenRouter deal (last week's watch item); Stripe is rolling up founder infrastructure fast.

signals.title: Climate tech VC funding up 55% to $26bn in H1'26, driven by data centers
signals.summary: Climate-tech subwatch: the funding jump is mostly AI datacenter power/cooling infrastructure, not consumer climate products; seed rounds are getting more selective, funded on proven demand and defensibility.

signals.title: Launch HN: Risklytics (YC S26), insurance brokerage for frontier tech companies
signals.summary: 52-point YC S26 launch; a niche insurance broker wedge for AI-labs-adjacent companies.

signals.title: Wikipedia pageviews on 'AI agent' more than doubled over the last 30 days
signals.summary: Daily views rose from 1,087 (2026-07-27) to 2,555 (2026-08-26) while 'Large language model' and 'Generative artificial intelligence' pageviews held flat or dipped, a public-attention signal specifically on agents, not AI generally.
